$comment: Contract for assets/ui/components.css and presentation.css. `ui.ts show <name>` prints an entry; `ui.ts check` lints pages against it; tests/ui.test.ts fails when this file and the CSS disagree. Using these components is optional: a page may style itself. `mode` is static (no JavaScript), or both (a static form plus an interactive layer from `script`).

root.use: Page base: background, text colour, base font and size from the theme.

card.children: optional first child <h3> is the small caps label
card.use: A note or aside. `focus` tints it with the accent for the one card that matters.
card.snippet:
The point

One or two sentences.

badge.use: Short uppercase status label inline with text.

table.children: `hl` and `dim` go on <tr> (highlight or de-emphasise a row) or on one <td>/<th>; `compact` goes on the table and sets monospace cells
table.use: Data table with a header row of <th>.

button.use: Native <button>; `outline` is the quiet variant, `loading` dims it and shows a busy cursor (put the busy text in the label yourself, such as "Deleting…"), the disabled attribute dims it.

alert.use: Callout with a coloured outline; `destructive` for errors.

flow.use: Row of steps. Does not wrap; keep to about five nodes at 1280px.

node.use: A step box. `hot` marks the changed step, `opt` (dashed) a step that only sometimes runs.

chip.use: One value in a box. It is large (1.22em) and does not wrap, so use it for values, not inside running text; use <b> or <span class="ui-mono"> there. `accent` colours it, `dashed` dashes it.

mono.use: Inline monospace for code and values.

reveal.children: elements with the data-step attribute, revealed one per click or Enter/Space; in a deck, one per → before the next slide
reveal.use: Show a list or sequence one step at a time. Static form: every step visible.

toggle.children: panels are direct children with a data-label attribute; the script adds the .ui-toggle-bar buttons
toggle.use: Switch between panels such as before and after. Static form: all panels stacked, each under its label.

trace.children:
a 
 with the code, an 
 and an  for the data going in, then one 
 per step (an 
 title, a

trace.use: Show real data going into a piece of code and coming out, one meaningful step at a time. Build it with scripts/trace.ts so each output is captured from a real run, not typed. Static form: every step stacked. On a slide give it the whole slide and keep each output to about 6 lines.

mock.children: <header> is the title bar (shows a close mark; `no-x` hides it), direct <div> children are the body, <footer> holds .ui-button actions; `closed` fades and dashes the whole mock to show a dialog that has been dismissed (it can read as disabled, so caption it); put an error or note in the body with .ui-alert
mock.use: Draw the dialog or prompt a slide talks about, so the reader sees it instead of imagining it. One mock per state; change it per step.

ref.use: A link that names its target and jumps to it. In a deck the slide ids are s1, s2, …; use href="#s4". Prefer it to "next slide" or "above". Also use it on a number to jump to where the number came from (give the target an id); with ui.js linked, the target flashes for 1.6 s.

status.children: a shape and a word, for example ▲Critical; nodata draws a dashed outline
status.use: A status as a shape and a word, never colour alone. Use ▲ critical, ◆ warning, ● normal, ◌ no data.

range.children: a .ui-range-bar holding .ui-range-span and an optional .ui-range-pin (data-label is its text), then .ui-range-lo and .ui-range-hi with the end values
range.use: One range on an axis shared with other bars, with an optional marker line. --lo, --hi and --at are percentages along the axis; do not compute them by hand: run scripts/figures.ts range.
range.snippet: 64.778.4

waffle.children: one <i> per cell, class "on" on the filled ones; --cols sets the columns (default 20)
waffle.use: A grid of 100 cells showing one percentage of a whole. Give it role="img" and an aria-label that states the value. Build it with scripts/figures.ts waffle so the count is exact.

cases.use: Small multiples: several cases that share one shape, side by side at one scale.

case.children: a <small> label with the inputs, a <b> with the result, then a ui-status

choice.children:
a naming the group (a inside it can show the chosen option's full name) and a
of , one per option
choice.use: A visible choice among a few named values, up to about 12. Every option is on screen, so nothing opens over the page the way a drop-down menu does. Native radios, so arrow keys and forms work; a disabled fieldset dims the options and clears the highlight.
choice.snippet: WR status

nav.children: one <a href="#id"> per section, then an optional <button> such as a theme switch
nav.use: A section menu that stays at the top of a long page. Give the <nav> an aria-label. Static form: plain sticky links. With ui.js: the link of the section in view gets aria-current="true". Use it when a page has three or more sections.
nav.snippet: WhyHowTry it

work.children: one <section> per step: a <header> with an <h3> title (no number; the CSS numbers the steps) and a <b> result, then a <div> with a <pre data-label="Formula"> and an <output data-label="With your numbers">
work.use: A worked calculation: for each step the result, the formula, then the formula with the reader's numbers put in. Static form: every step stacked. With ui.js: Back, Next, Replay and Show all, arrow keys on the buttons, a dot on a rail, and later steps dimmed. The numbers must come from a run or from a model tested against the real code (see references/live-model.md).

replay.children:
a .ui-replay-axis (role="img", an aria-label, one numbered tick per event, N the percent along the axis, class done on each in the static form) followed by one
per event: a
with an

saying why it happened, and an optional with the state that results
replay.use: Events in time order, one at a time. Each event says what happened and why. Ticks are evenly spaced, so the axis shows order, not duration; put durations in the text. Static form: every event stacked. With ui.js: Back, Next and Play, arrow keys on the buttons, click or Enter on a tick, a marker that slides. It opens on the last event. Build it with scripts/figures.ts replay (see references/motion.md).

layout.$comment: Slide layout classes from presentation.css. Only meaningful inside the deck stage.

slide.use: One slide. The first carries `on`. Direct child of #stage.

eyebrow.use: Small caps line above a title.

foot.use: Footer pinned to the bottom: source on the left, `n / N` on the right. N must equal the slide count.

big.use: A single large number in the heading font.
